chunks: From him, from al-‘Abbās, from Ibn al-Mughīrah, from ‘Abd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Abī ‘Abd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

A man led a people in prayer while he was junub, and he had performed tayammum, while they were in a state of taharah. He said: “There is no harm. So when a man performs tayammum, let that be at the end of the time, for if water escapes him, the earth will not escape him.”

key_terms.آخِرِ وَقْتٍ: The end portion of the prescribed prayer time.
key_terms.الْأَرْضُ: Earth or ground, the basis for tayammum.
key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: Performed tayammum as a substitute for wudu or ghusl when water is unavailable.
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: A person in a state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl.
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem or legal objection.

ai.seo_question: Can a person in janabah who performed tayammum lead others in salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on tayammum for one in janabah who leads others in salat while the followers are in a state of taharah. It affirms the validity of such leadership and instructs that tayammum should be delayed until the end of the prayer time, since if water is unavailable, earth for tayammum remains available.
